status: Reproduced packet-interleaving input fault with Sample Locks absent. Hardware incident attribution and fix qualification remain open.
method: The unchanged development base ran on a copied disposable card. A fader report was delivered through emulated UART1 in two pieces; a real USB development KEY request was inserted between them. To construct one-byte arrivals using the emulator two-byte key command, a dummy leading byte was removed from the emulated receive FIFO while execution was paused, before firmware ran. No firmware or project-memory bytes were patched.

interleavedFuncRelease.precondition: FUNC held normally: held row bit set and stock key state 2.

interpretation: The development input implementation can corrupt packet framing without any module installed.
The unintended TRIG5-7 state matches the hardware readback exactly; missed FUNC release is also reproduced.
This is a strong mechanism-level explanation for the hardware incident, not proof of every unintended hardware edit or any saturation threshold.
limitations: No DSP execution, audible-output assertion or hardware timing qualification in this reproduction.
Model transport did not advance in the no-DSP setup; successful STOP or the exact paste message is not claimed here.
The deliberate split widens the interleaving window; no physical occurrence rate or latency bound is inferred.
No input-path fix, fresh hardware rerun, source runtime change, Keep, flash or publication occurred.
attemptsNotCountedAsPass: Default boot instruction budget ended before startup; increased for later attempts.
DSP-enabled startup was stopped to focus on UI/input isolation.
An early helper tried a nonexistent Bench.close method; no clean pass was claimed.
A first split-byte method required a parked main context and was refused before injection; the UART FIFO construction replaced it.
